en: The Questions of King Milinda,
Chapter on Mindfulness, 3.
The Question on the Marks of a Great Man (Mahāpurisalakkhaṇapañha)
The King said:

"Venerable Nāgasena, is the Buddha endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, golden-hued, with skin like refined gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance?

"Yes, Great King, the Blessed One is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, golden-hued, with skin like refined gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance."

“But, Bhante, were his mother and father also endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, graced with the eighty minor characteristics, golden-hued, with skin like gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance?

“No, great king, his mother and father were not endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, nor graced with the eighty minor characteristics, nor were they golden-hued, with skin like gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance.”
“If that were so, venerable Nāgasena, a Buddha would not arise— one endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man,
adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, golden-hued, with skin like refined gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance; rather,
a son would be like his mother or belong to his mother’s side, or a son would be like his father.”
“Or is there a side of fathers?
The Elder said:
“But, Great King, is there any lotus with a hundred petals?”
“Yes, venerable sir, there is.
“But from what does it originate?
“It is born in the mud and grows in the water.”
“Great King, is the lotus similar to mud in its color, fragrance, or taste?
“No, venerable sir.
“Then is it similar to water in its fragrance or taste?”
“No indeed, Bhante.

“In the same way, Great King, the Blessed One is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics, golden-hued, with skin like refined gold, and possessing a fathom-wide radiance; yet it would not be so for him...”
“Your parents were endowed with the thirty-two marks of a Great Man, adorned with the eighty minor characteristics,
golden-hued, with skin like refined gold, and possessing a fathom-wide aura.
“Excellent, venerable Nāgasena!”
The third question on the marks of a Great Man.
